title: Sun Day
lede: Can one sunny spot grow food and make energy? Set up a solar panel above a seedling, guess what will happen, then run a sunny Arizona day and see how your plant and your panel did.
estimates: The numbers are estimates for learning, not measurements.
needName: Add your name first. Your Sun Day runs are saved with your Planting Log.
whoLink: Not you? Pick your name on the Planting Log.

run.done: Results are ready. Sun Score: {total} out of 200.
run.saved: Saved to My Sun Day runs.

loads.both: fan, and pump with a water tank

gauges.atSunrise: These show your setup at sunrise. Run the day to watch them change.

controls.step1: 1 · Pick a plant and a day
controls.panelHint: Bigger panels make more energy, and more shade.
controls.heightHint: A high panel lets more light in from the sides.
controls.turnOn: Turn on one, both or neither
controls.waterPump: The pump waters the plant by itself when the soil gets dry. It needs strong sun and a big panel.
controls.waterHand: Without the pump, you water the plant once each morning.

cropHints.lettuce: Likes cool weather and some shade.
cropHints.chili: Loves sun and handles heat well.

predict.prompt: Compared with the same plant in full sun with no panel, your plant will grow…

why.pump: the pump keeps the soil wet

predict.skipDay: Skip prediction and run the day
predict.skipWeek: Skip prediction and run the week
predict.skipAgain: Skip prediction and run it again

results.title: Your Sun Score
results.ref: A plot with no panel scores {fs}. Beat it by sharing the sun.
results.note: The line on the Food bar marks a plant in full sun with no panel. Food is out of a perfect day. Energy is out of the best panel setup.
results.skipped: You skipped the prediction this time.
results.what: Your {crop} grew {food}% of {perfect}. A full-sun plant grew {fs}%. Your panel made {wh} Wh, which is {energy}% of the best setup.

heat.name: Challenge 1: Beat the heat
heat.goal: Heat wave week with basil. Grow at least twice as much as basil with no panel.
heat.pass: Your basil grew more than twice the no-panel basil.
heat.fail: Your basil needs more protection from the heat.

fan.name: Challenge 2: Fan all afternoon
fan.goal: Sunny day. Keep the fan spinning every hour from noon to 5 pm, and grow at least as much as a plant with no panel.
fan.pass: The fan ran all afternoon and the plant kept up.
fan.fail: The fan stopped in the afternoon, or the plant fell behind.

tank.name: Challenge 3: Water by itself all week
tank.goal: Sunny week with the pump and no hand watering. The soil may be dry for 30 hours at most.
tank.pass: The soil stayed just right all week.
tank.fail: The soil got too dry. Try slowing down how fast it dries.

lowLight.why: Your {crop} got about {light}% of the sun under the panels. It wanted more light to grow fast.
lowLight.next: How could you give the plant more light and still make energy?
hints: Light can sneak in from the sides.
A high panel lets more side light in. A smaller panel makes less shade.
Try the panel set high, or the small panel.

hotShade.why: Leaves were above {hi} °F for {hours} sunny hours. That is too warm for {crop} to grow well.
hotShade.next: What could shade the plant during the hottest hours?
hints: When is the sun strongest? What is above the plant then?
A bigger panel makes more shade, and shade cools the leaves.
Try the big panel or both panels.

hotFan.why: Leaves were above {hi} °F for {hours} sunny hours. That is too warm for {crop} to grow well.
hotFan.next: Your panel makes power. What could it run to cool the leaves?
hints: Moving air carries heat away from the leaves.
A running fan cools the leaves by a few degrees.
Turn on the fan.

hotHeight.why: Leaves were above {hi} °F for {hours} sunny hours. That is too warm for {crop} to grow well.
hotHeight.next: How could hot air escape from under the panel?
hints: Hot air gets trapped under a low panel.
A high panel lets hot air out and side light in.
Set the panel high.

hotPlant.why: Leaves were above {hi} °F for {hours} sunny hours. That is too warm for {crop} to grow well.
hotPlant.next: Your setup already gives shade and wind. Which plant handles heat best?
hints: Some plants like it hot. Read the hint under each plant.
Chili pepper handles heat better than lettuce or basil.
Try chili pepper with the same setup.

hotMax.why: Leaves were above {hi} °F for {hours} sunny hours. Even chili pepper grows slowly when it is that hot.
hotMax.next: This heat is tough for any plant. Did your setup still beat the plant with no panel?
hints: Look at the line on the Food bar.
Shade, a high panel and the fan each cool the leaves a little.
Compare your score with the no-panel score above.

dry.why: The soil got too dry for {dry} sunny hours. Thirsty plants stop growing.
dry.next: How could the soil stay wet longer during the day?
hints: Where does the water go on a hot afternoon?
Shade slows drying. The pump only runs when the panel has power left after the fan.
Try both panels with the pump on and the fan off.

tankEmpty.why: The tank ran dry on day {day} at {hour}:00, then the soil dried out.
tankEmpty.next: How could the same water last longer?
hints: Where does the water go on a hot day?
Shade slows drying, so the same water lasts longer.
Try both panels with the pump on.

lowEnergy.why: Your plant did well, but your panel made only {energy}% of the energy the best setup can make.
lowEnergy.next: Can you make more energy and still keep the plant happy?
hints: Which panel catches the most sun?
More panel area means more energy, but also more shade.
Try both panels set high.

noPanel.why: Your plant grew fine in full sun, but with no panel you made no energy.
noPanel.next: What happens to the plant if you add a panel above it?
hints: Shade can help or hurt. It depends on the plant and the heat.
Try a small panel first, then compare.
Try the big panel set high.

balanced.why: A good balance: nothing held the plant back much, and the panel made {energy}% of the best energy.
balanced.next: Can you raise one score without dropping the other?
hints: Change just one thing, then run again and compare.
Try the other panel height, or a different panel size.
Compare Big + high with Both + high.
